Distal tubule
The distal tubule, like the TAL of the loop of Henle is not permeable to water, but mainly a site of ion reabsorption. Also here the
major driving force for sodium reabsorption is the Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase on the basolateral membrane. By extruding sodium from the cell
into the interstitium it creates the gradient that leads to Naþ absorption from the luminal side. This process happens through the
NaCl cotransporter (NCC), which is sensitive to thiazide diuretics.
